analysis.title: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN): Q3'26 Earnings First Take
key_insights: GS expects an initial negative share reaction to Amazon's Q3 2026 report: results were neutral to slightly weaker than GS/Street estimates across most of the business.

AWS revenue of $45.98bn (+39.3% YoY) and Advertising were ahead of GS/Street estimates but below buyside expectations of 42%+ AWS YoY growth, which had been a consistent topic in the weeks before the report.
Q3'26 total revenue was $201.94bn (+12.1% YoY) vs GSe $201.51bn, Visible Alpha Street est. $202.35bn and guidance of $197.0-202.0bn.
Q3'26 GAAP operating income was $28.1bn (13.9% margin) vs GSe $26.04bn, Street est. $26.16bn and guidance of $22.5-26.5bn, a beat of about $2.0bn vs both GS and Street.

Q4'26 revenue guide of $240-247bn (includes a 60bps FX headwind) brackets Street est. of $244.4bn (GSe $241.4bn). Q4 GAAP operating income guide of $28.5-33.5bn has a high end slightly above Street est. of $32.9bn (GSe $32.0bn).
Management commentary pointed to AWS growth of +40% for 2027 and 2028.
Amazon reaffirmed about $220bn of capex for 2026.
Online Stores revenue grew only +1.6% YoY to $68.47bn, vs Third-Party Seller Services +9.4%, Subscription Services +11.4% and Advertising +10.9%.
AWS operating income was $17.77bn (38.7% margin), North America $8.72bn (7.7% margin) and International $1.58bn (3.7% margin).

GS expects earnings call questions on: AWS in the broader AI theme over the next 6-12 months and compute capacity coming online vs visible demand, Bedrock and Trainium positioning, consumer health, agentic commerce, and capital needs and funding for compute.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps a Buy and a $375 12-month target based on a sum-of-the-parts using EV/EBIT for North America and AWS and EV/Sales for International, on NTM+1 estimates. The report cites 47.3% upside from the $254.60 close on 28 Oct 2026, although it also expects an initial negative share reaction.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported (GAAP) total revenue $201.94bn (+12.1% YoY) vs GSe $201.51bn, Visible Alpha Street est. $202.35bn and guidance of $197.0-202.0bn.
Q3'26 reported GAAP operating income $28.1bn (13.9% margin) vs GSe $26.04bn, Street est. $26.16bn and guidance of $22.5-26.5bn.

Q3'26 reported segment revenue: Online Stores $68.47bn (+1.6% YoY), Third-Party Seller Services $46.49bn (+9.4%), Subscription Services $14.01bn (+11.4%), Advertising $19.64bn (+10.9%), AWS $45.98bn (+39.3%), Other $1.65bn (+16.3%), North America $112.85bn (+6.2%), International $43.11bn (+5.4%).
Q3'26 reported GAAP operating income by segment: North America $8.72bn (7.7% margin), International $1.58bn (3.7% margin), AWS $17.77bn (38.7% margin).

Q4'26 guidance: revenue $240-247bn (includes a 60bps FX headwind) vs GSe $241.4bn and Street est. $244.4bn. GAAP operating income $28.5-33.5bn vs GSe $32.0bn and Street est. $32.9bn, a 12.7% GAAP operating margin at the midpoint vs GSe 13.3% and Street est. 13.5%.
Management reaffirmed about $220bn of 2026 capex and commented on AWS growth of +40% for 2027 and 2028.

GS estimates: FY2026E revenue $825,055mn, EBIT $109,373mn, EPS $12.76. FY2027E revenue $962,384.5mn, EBIT $152,250.4mn, EPS $10.99. FY2028E revenue $1,100,176.3mn, EBIT $197,147.8mn, EPS $14.02. The 9/26E quarterly EPS shown is $1.90.
risk_factors: Competition affecting eCommerce or Cloud growth.
Lack of success in scaling higher-margin businesses: Advertising, Cloud, third-party selling and subscriptions.
Investments across initiatives creating a headwind to gross or operating margin.
Product or platform changes needed to comply with changes in the global regulatory environment.
Exposure to global macroeconomic volatility and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
Capital needs and the funding of compute spending, including the roughly $220bn 2026 capex. GS models negative FCF yield of (1.6)% for 2026E and (2.1)% for 2027E.
vol_and_positioning: Buyside expectations of 42%+ YoY AWS growth were a consistent topic in the weeks before the report. AWS grew +39.3%, below that bar, which is the basis for GS's expected initial negative share reaction.
